bracket: [Textbook misprint in a distractor: one alternative is printed as \(\vec{A} \times (\vec{B} + \vec{C}) = \vec{A} \times \vec{B} + \vec{B} \times \vec{C}\), where the second term should read \(\vec{A} \times \vec{C}\). Taken literally that statement is also incorrect, so as printed the question has two answers. The keyed answer is nevertheless the intended one and is not in doubt: the option set is built as three true identities and one false, the false one being that the cross product commutes, and this chapter prints the distributive law correctly at Eq. (2.21) with \(\vec{A} \times \vec{C}\). The stem is preserved as printed rather than repaired, so a reader who spots the typo can see it.]

[Textbook misprint: the stem prints the position vector as \(\vec{r} = 4\hat{i} \times 6\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}\), with a multiplication sign where a plus belongs — the same line prints an unambiguous plus in the momentum vector, so the two glyphs are distinguishable on the page. Read literally, \((4\hat{i}) \times (6\hat{j}) = 24\hat{k}\) would give \(\vec{r} = 21\hat{k}\), which matches neither the determinant the book then writes (whose first row is 4, 6, −3) nor its printed answer. The stem is preserved as printed and solved as the book's own working intends. Its closing line also sets an arrow over \(k\) where the other unit vectors carry hats.]
